pages.title: The last night at the Grand Hotel
pages.story:
One hotel. One last party. One guest too many.
You are the Grand Hotel’s new night manager. Tomorrow it closes forever. Tonight, every room is full, the mountain road is disappearing under snow, and the owner has promised a surprise at midnight.
Sherpa Tensing takes your bag. “A hotel is like a mountain,” he says. “The difficult part is knowing who to trust.” Behind him, someone is watching from a window on a floor that does not exist.

pages.title: Something outside the routine
pages.story:
Alice is teaching you the evening routine. Mrs Hudson checks the guest book. Holmes and Watson, who run the village investigation office, are here for dinner, not work.
“The owner rings the desk every evening,” Alice says. “But look at his light. Someone is calling from his office right now.”
You answer. A voice whispers, “Don’t let them sell the hotel.” Then the line dies.
pages.question: Describe the routine, then the action happening now: “The owner ___ every evening. Someone ___ from his office right now.”
why: Both forms look back to the past, but this sentence describes a routine and the present moment.
A completed result and a finished past event do not express these two meanings.
This reverses the meanings: an evening routine is simple; the call happening now is continuous.
Every evening gives a routine: present simple. Right now gives an action in progress: present continuous.

pages.title: A key without a room
pages.story:
Count Blocula, the hotel’s owner, arrives in an ivory dinner jacket. He gives you a brass key marked 309. “Keep this safe until I return.”
Rabbit, the fast-moving bellhop, insists there are only two guest floors. Mouse, the smallest porter, nods. Security chief Lestrade checks the printed plan. No room 309.
“I saw that key yesterday,” Lestrade says. “But this is the first time the Count has given it to anyone.”
pages.question: One event has a finished time; the other matters now: “Lestrade ___ the key yesterday. The Count ___ it to us, so we have it now.”
why: Has been giving suggests an ongoing or repeated activity, not one completed handover.
Saw describes the completed sighting. A routine gives does not fit the one new handover.
Yesterday is a finished past time, so use saw, not has seen.
Yesterday takes past simple. Has just given presents a recent completed action with a present result: we have the key.

pages.title: Eleven seconds of darkness
pages.story:
Zombiella reaches the last note of her song. Tito is at the piano. Blane, the night porter, carries a tray of glasses. Andreas, the hotel’s buyer, watches the owner instead of the stage.
The lights go out. A tray crashes. Eleven seconds later, light returns.
Blocula’s chair is empty. An ivory envelope lies on the floor. Inside it you find a note: “At midnight, tell them what this building is really worth.”
pages.question: Set the background, then name the interruption: “Zombiella ___ when the lights suddenly ___ out.”
why: Past continuous sets the action already in progress. Past simple marks the event that interrupted it.
Had sung would mean the song was already finished; she was still singing.
The sudden blackout is the short event, not the background action.
Has sung does not set an action in progress at that past moment.

pages.title: The first impossible alibi
pages.story:
Andreas says he left the ballroom at 20:10, after the blackout, and went directly to the terrace. He claims he has never used the service lift.
Zombiella shows you a photo Rabbit took at 20:03. Andreas’s chair is empty. His coat is already gone. Tito remembers opening the service door for him before the lights failed.
“A confident voice is not a clock,” Holmes says. “Put the events in order.”
pages.question: The photo is at 20:03; the blackout is at 20:05: “Andreas ___ the ballroom before the lights ___ out.”
why: Have gone links to now, but the reference point here is 20:05.
Present perfect does not look back from this finished past reference point.
Had already left marks the earlier event. Went marks the later blackout. His claimed departure time is false.
The sentence reconstructs two finished past events, not a present routine.

clue.title: The 20:03 photograph
clue.text: Andreas had already left before the 20:05 blackout. His claimed 20:10 departure is false.

pages.title: The man inside the lift
pages.story:
You find Zombito waist-deep in an open control cabinet. Jax holds a lamp. The Creature, the hotel’s enormous maintenance assistant, is supporting the lift door with one hand.
Zombito looks alarming and sounds exhausted. “I started at seven. I’m still fixing this thing. I’ve replaced three fuses, but the door sensor keeps failing.”
There is a second fault: someone has removed a page from the lift’s paper log.
pages.question: Focus first on ongoing effort, then completed results: “Zombito ___ since seven. He ___ three fuses so far.”
why: Worked presents a finished period; was replacing does not count completed fuses.
Has worked can describe duration, but has been replacing does not clearly count three completed results.
Has been working emphasises the activity continuing up to now. Has replaced counts three completed results.
Is working alone does not express since seven; replaced loses the explicit up-to-now viewpoint.

pages.title: The kitchen knows everyone
pages.story:
Chef Mrs Hudson has sent Rafa, Silver and Jack to feed the frightened guests. Kit is checking meal deliveries. Henry Clerval, the hotel doctor’s assistant, makes tea for anyone who looks ready to faint.
“I’ve known Andreas for ten years,” Hudson says. “He smiles like a man selling you your own shoes.”
Kit has counted every dinner tray. One extra meal went to the old east annex. Nobody has booked a room there.
The Queen, the retired chairwoman, has sent her untouched pudding back. The Time Warden wants the staff to finish on schedule. Mrs Hudson ignores them both.
pages.question: Choose a lasting state and an ongoing activity: “Hudson ___ Andreas for ten years. Kit ___ the deliveries all evening and is still checking.”
why: Use present perfect simple with the state know. Use present perfect continuous to emphasise checking over a period up to now.
These past forms move both facts away from the current investigation.
Know normally avoids the continuous. Checked would present the activity as finished.
Know is normally a state, so we do not usually say is knowing. Checks gives a routine rather than tonight’s ongoing activity.

pages.title: The recording that arrived late
pages.story:
Lestrade’s camera uploads clips slowly in the storm. At 20:18, a recording finally arrived. It shows Blocula walking into the service lift at 20:04, carrying a folder.
Blane insists he saw Andreas enter the same lift at 20:02. The camera confirms it. Andreas was already inside when the Count arrived.
Watson notices something else: the Count is smiling. He expected a meeting, not a kidnapping.
pages.question: Report the order from a later past viewpoint: “By the time the Count ___ at 20:04, Andreas ___ the lift at 20:02.”
why: Arrived gives the later reference point. Had entered takes us back to the earlier event.
Enters is present; the whole sequence is being reconstructed in the past.
Both events have finished clock times in the past.
This puts the past perfect on the later event instead of the earlier entry.

pages.title: A page in the rubbish
pages.story:
Victor Frankenstein, the hotel doctor, arrives with retired engineer Professor Waldman. Neither likes the smell of hot wires.
The Creature finds the missing log page under a bin. The lift travelled to “E-309” at 20:06. The passenger doors opened, then someone locked the annex door from outside.
Zombito explains his own movements: he started repairing the panel at 19:00 and was still working there when the alarm rang at 20:05. Jax and the Creature were with him.
pages.question: Look back from the alarm, then describe what was in progress: “Zombito ___ for over an hour when the alarm rang. At that moment, he ___ the panel.”
why: Has checked describes a result linked to now rather than a past action in progress.
Had been repairing measures an activity continuing up to a past event. Was checking places us inside that activity.
These forms use now as the viewpoint; the reference point is a past alarm.
Had checked means the checking was already complete, but it was still happening.

clue.title: The torn lift log
clue.text: The lift reached E-309 at 20:06. Zombito was repairing the panel with two witnesses when the alarm rang.

pages.title: Which witness gets your trust?
pages.story:
Zombiella says Andreas paid her to keep singing until 20:15, even if the lights failed. She thought it was a strange joke. Alice admits she copied an old annex key for him yesterday because he claimed the Count had asked for it.
Both are frightened of losing their jobs. Both could help you.
You can ask Zombiella to search for the payment receipt, or ask Alice to trace the copied key. Your partner will bring a different piece of supporting evidence later.
pages.question: Contrast a finished mistake with a problem that remains: “Alice ___ the key yesterday. Since then, she ___ unable to stop worrying.”
why: Copies describes a habit; is alone does not carry the since-then meaning.
These forms do not express one completed copying event and a state continuing to now.
Yesterday takes past simple. Has been connects her state from then to now.
Has copied does not combine with yesterday in this finished-event use.

choice.prompt: Choose your partner. Both routes keep all 30 pages.

options.label: Trust Zombiella · find the payment
options.effect: Her receipt will expose how the distraction was arranged.

options.label: Trust Alice · trace the copied key
options.effect: Her key record will show who requested access to the annex.

pages.title: The gardeners’ secret
pages.story:
Eira and Lina run the winter garden. Bram maintains the outside paths. Nim, their small stone-faced assistant, has been hiding biscuits in the planters. Rook, Bram’s shaggy mountain dog, has found every one.
“We’ve visited the annex before,” Lina says. “But we went there last Tuesday for the old garden plans.”
Eira points across the lake. The annex is below the ballroom, hidden by trees. The windows you saw from outside belong to it.
pages.question: Separate experience from one dated visit: “The sisters ___ the annex before. They ___ there last Tuesday.”
why: Neither an action happening now nor present perfect fits the dated second clause.
Go changes the dated visit into a present routine.
Have visited gives experience up to now. Went gives the specific finished visit.
Have gone does not fit the finished time last Tuesday.

pages.title: A light below the waterline
pages.story:
Nemo runs the hotel’s lake boats. Professor Aronnax is studying the water; Nadia, Mara and Lia maintain his instruments.
Nadia’s sensor shows the annex heating has stopped. Someone could be trapped in a room that is getting colder every minute. Mara has repaired the emergency boat engine. Lia is still searching for its spare battery.
Through the rain, you see three flashes from a low window. Then three more. Someone is asking for help.
pages.question: Choose the completed repair and the unfinished search: “Mara ___ the engine; it works now. Lia ___ for the battery for twenty minutes and is still looking.”
why: Has been repairing does not clearly confirm the completed repair; has found would mean the search succeeded.
The first form leaves the repair in progress at a past moment; the search is still continuing now.
Has repaired foregrounds the finished result. Has been searching foregrounds continuing effort up to now.
Repairs describes a routine and searched presents a finished search.

pages.title: The hotel’s “ghosts”
pages.story:
Angus Tulloch, the boatman, and Dr Vass, the lake biologist, have brought guests in from the storm. Harbour officer Brannan is checking their names. Kirsty and Ewan Sinclair carry blankets while Sandy Weir ties up the boats.
“White shapes in the annex!” Sinclair says. “Ghosts!”
Vass holds up a bedsheet. Staff have been moving old linen through the tunnel. Tulloch heard someone knocking behind the archive door, but the music upstairs drowned it out.
The Docherty brothers secure the landing. Davie counts arrivals with the visiting sergeant. The Lennox family confirm the annex heating failed.
pages.question: Explain the apparently empty landing: “When Brannan reached the landing, Tulloch ___ the guests inside. While Brannan checked their names, Vass ___ blankets.”
why: Has taken uses a present viewpoint, not the earlier action before Brannan arrived.
The guests were already inside, and Vass’s giving was in progress during the checking.
Present forms do not reconstruct this past sequence.
Past perfect explains what happened before arrival; past continuous describes the parallel activity during the checking.

pages.title: The floor that never vanished
pages.story:
Tensing opens a cabinet of old plans. Walton, the hotel’s retired transport captain, remembers the numbering. The annex once had three levels of its own. Its bottom room was 309. Renovations joined that level to the main hotel’s basement.
The Clockmaker, who maintains the lobby clock, knows the tunnel. Mouse can reach its narrow latch.
“I used to deliver bags there,” Tensing says. “Dark tunnels don’t worry me. I’m used to working in them.”
pages.question: Choose a past habit that ended, then something familiar now: “Tensing ___ deliver bags to the annex. He ___ working in dark tunnels.”
why: Used to + base verb expresses a former habit. Be used to + -ing expresses familiarity. These are different constructions.
Would can express repeated past actions, but has used to working is not the familiarity construction.
Neither was using to nor uses to forms these meanings.
Is used to needs a noun or -ing form; used to working is not the past-habit pattern.

pages.title: Room 309
pages.story:
Cat, the hotel’s silent night cleaner, emerges from behind a shelf and nearly gives Watson a heart attack. “The door’s been locked since eight,” she says. “I heard the Count call for help.”
You slide your key into the outer door. It opens onto a passage. A second door has an electronic lock. Through its small window, Blocula holds up a folder: STAFF OWNERSHIP.
He did not plan to sell everyone’s jobs. He planned to give the staff control of the hotel.
pages.question: Describe a state continuing to now, then the earlier locking: “The door ___ locked since eight. Someone ___ it before Cat came down.”
why: Was does not carry the state through to now; locks gives a routine.
Is alone does not express the since-eight duration, and has locked does not locate the locking before a past visit.
Had been stops the duration at a past viewpoint; is locking says it is happening now.
Has been links the locked state to now. Had locked places the locking before Cat’s past arrival.

clue.title: The staff-ownership folder
clue.text: Blocula is alive inside archive E-309. His folder concerns staff ownership, giving the buyer a motive to stop him.

pages.title: The midnight clause
pages.story:
Blocula speaks through the glass. “Andreas asked me to inspect the old plans. He locked me in. He took my phone.”
The folder contains the original staff-ownership agreement. A copy must reach the village registrar before midnight to cancel the sale. Manager Menzies, who arranged the deal, has told everyone the deadline cannot move.
The Count points to a second document: a structural survey declaring the hotel unsafe. Waldman says its measurements are impossible.
pages.question: Choose an action in progress at a future time, then one completed before it: “At 23:30 the registrar ___ applications. By midnight, she ___ the office.”
options: will have checked / will be closing
will be checking / will have closed
why: This swaps the intended meanings: checking is in progress at 23:30; closing will be complete by midnight.
These forms do not describe the stated future times.
Will be checking puts us inside a future activity. Will have closed looks back from a future deadline at a completed action.
Has closed is a present result, not completion viewed from a future deadline.

pages.title: A promise in the storm
pages.story:
A branch hits the glass roof. Outside, the old footbridge bends under wet snow. Bram orders everyone away from it.
“Look at that beam,” Lina says. “It’s going to fall.” Eira grabs the first-aid bag. Tensing looks at your shaking hands and quietly offers to carry the folder when you get it out.
An expected event and a decision made now can both point to the future. They tell us different things about the speaker’s evidence and intention.
pages.question: Use the usual evidence-based prediction and immediate-offer forms: “Look at the bending beam! It ___. Don’t worry; I ___ the folder for you.”
options: is going to fall / will carry
why: Both verbs describe the past, not the prediction and offer.
Has fallen says the fall already happened, but the beam is still bending.
Falls gives a general or scheduled event; have carried looks back.
Going to fits the visible evidence. Will fits an offer made at the moment of speaking. In other contexts both future forms can overlap.

pages.title: The last cable car
pages.story:
Walton checks the emergency transport timetable. The last downhill cable car leaves at 23:40, provided the wind stays below the limit. After that, the only road will be under snow.
Jax has arranged to meet the registrar’s assistant at the lower station at 23:50. He shows you the confirmation on his phone.
The plan is tight, but possible. The real problem is getting Blocula and the original agreement out of the archive.
pages.question: Choose the timetable form and the personal arrangement: “The last car ___ at 23:40. Jax ___ the assistant at 23:50; they have confirmed it.”
why: Has met says the meeting is already complete.
Left is past, and will have met views the meeting as complete by a later future time.
Has left is a present result rather than tonight’s published departure.
Present simple commonly states a timetable. Present continuous commonly states a confirmed future arrangement.

pages.title: Two things worth saving
pages.story:
Nadia finds a backup socket. Zombito can power the archive lock from the workshop, but the damaged circuit cannot run the lock and the document scanner together.
Victor checks the temperature behind the glass. Blocula is shivering. Clerval prepares warm blankets. The Creature offers to hold the power cable in place.
Choose your priority: free the Count first, or scan the agreement first. Both can be done, but the first decision changes the rescue and the ending.
pages.question: Choose an activity under way at a future moment, then an existing plan: “At eleven, Zombito ___ the circuit. He ___ use the backup socket; that is his plan.”
options: will be testing / is going to
why: Has tested is a present result; will have use is not a valid verb phrase.
Will have tested makes the testing complete by then; the sentence asks for the activity in progress.
Future continuous puts the testing in progress at eleven. Going to states a plan already made.
These past forms do not describe the future testing and current plan.

options.label: The lock · get Blocula out first
options.effect: Protect the owner. The document can be scanned after the rescue.

options.label: The scanner · protect the agreement first
options.effect: Secure an early copy, but leave Blocula in the cold for longer.

pages.title: The longest shift
pages.story:
Nemo brings a boat battery to keep the lights alive. Mara and Lia run a cable through the service tunnel. Nadia checks the current while Zombito talks them through every connection.
“I started at seven,” he says. “At midnight I’ll have been working for five hours. Remind me never to accept an ‘easy’ evening shift again.”
You need a completed repair before the cable car leaves, not just five hours of effort.
pages.question: Contrast duration up to a future time with completion before a deadline: “At midnight, Zombito ___ for five hours. By 23:20, he ___ the lock circuit.”
options: will have been working / will have repaired
why: Future perfect continuous measures duration up to a future point. Future perfect simple presents the repair as complete by its deadline.
These forms use present and past viewpoints rather than the two future reference points.
Will be working places us inside the activity but does not measure the full duration up to midnight.
Will work does not express five hours accumulated by midnight; is repairing is present.

pages.title: The buyer’s real plan
pages.story:
Waldman and Aronnax compare the survey with the building plans. Andreas measured a storage wall as if it supported the whole hotel. Kit finds a second set of plans: luxury apartments, with no staff rooms.
Before anyone noticed the mistake, Andreas was going to use the “unsafe” report to close the hotel cheaply. He had already arranged tomorrow’s meeting with a developer.
The missing owner, the false report and the midnight deadline are parts of one scheme.
pages.question: Describe an intention held in the past, then an arrangement completed before discovery: “Andreas ___ close the hotel. He ___ the developer’s meeting before Waldman found the error.”
options: has been going to / was arranging
why: Will and arranges do not describe the earlier plan and prior completed arrangement.
Was going to reports a past intention. Had arranged marks a completed arrangement earlier than the discovery.
These present-linked forms do not match the requested past viewpoint.
Was arranging leaves the arrangement in progress rather than complete before discovery.

pages.title: Evidence from your partner
pages.story:
Your chosen partner returns, wet and breathless. The other has stayed with the worried guests, keeping Andreas from slipping away.
Holmes asks you to read the document aloud. “Evidence only helps if we say exactly what it proves.”
The archive lock is still being repaired. The false survey has already been copied and sent to Lestrade’s secure phone.
pages.question: Contrast an ongoing passive action and a completed passive result: “The lock ___ now. The false survey ___ already, so Lestrade has a copy.”
options: is being repaired / has been copied
why: The first is a finished past action; the second leaves the copy unfinished.
Is being repaired is present continuous passive: the work is ongoing. Has been copied is present perfect passive: the result is available now.
Is repaired can describe a state or routine; was being copied does not confirm the copy is finished.
These active forms incorrectly make the lock and survey the agents doing the work.

variants.zombiella: Zombiella unfolds a signed receipt. Andreas paid for a song to continue until 20:15, leaving himself time to reach the annex unnoticed. The receipt proves a planned distraction; the camera and lift log connect it to his movements.
variants.alice: Alice brings the signed key request. Andreas asked for access to E-309 at 19:55, although he later claimed never to have used the service lift. The signature connects him to the copied annex key.

pages.title: When the green light comes on
pages.story:
The circuit hums. Zombito raises one hand: nobody touches the door until its light turns green. The Creature braces the frame. Victor waits with blankets.
Your earlier decision sets the order of events, but you still need a safe, clear instruction. A wrong tense could make the command sound as if the rescue has already happened.
Beyond the glass, Blocula stands back. He trusts you to get this right.
pages.question: Give the real future instruction: “When the light ___ green, we ___ the door.”
why: Opened is past, so the instruction no longer describes what you will do next.
In this future time clause after when, use present simple rather than will.
Use present simple after when for a future time condition, then will + base verb in the main clause.
These past and present-perfect forms do not give the intended future instruction.

variants.people: You sent the first burst of power to the lock. Blocula will be brought out before you turn on the scanner. Victor approves. “A document can wait five minutes. A person should not have to.”
variants.paper: You sent the first burst of power to the scanner. The agreement is safe, but Blocula has spent longer in the cold. Victor prepares to treat him as soon as the lock releases.

pages.title: The signature under the dust
pages.story:
The lock clicks. Blocula steps out, shaking but alive. Elizabeth, the staff representative, and Justine, head housekeeper, meet him with a coat. Watson checks the original agreement.
It was signed last month, before Andreas offered to buy the hotel. The sale contract only applies if no earlier staff agreement is registered by midnight. That is why Andreas needed the Count silent tonight.
Under the dust is the final page: every permanent member of staff owns a share.
William brings his sister Elizabeth a mug of tea and asks whether she will still have a job tomorrow. “That is exactly what we’re deciding,” she says.
pages.question: Put the legal documents in order without changing their timing: “The staff ___ the agreement last month. By the time Andreas made his offer, Blocula ___ it too.”
why: Were signing leaves the signing in progress; has signed uses now as the reference point.
Is signing would put Blocula’s signature in progress now, contrary to the old document.
Signed belongs to the finished time last month. Had signed marks Blocula’s completed signature before the later offer.
Last month takes a finished past form; signs is present.

clue.title: The earlier signed agreement
clue.text: The staff and Blocula signed before Andreas made his offer. Registering the agreement before midnight will stop the sale.

pages.title: The whole night, in order
pages.story:
Lestrade asks Andreas to stay. Blane stands by the door; Tito stops playing. Menzies admits he accepted the false survey without asking an independent engineer to check it.
You lay out the sequence: Andreas entered the lift at 20:02. Blocula joined him at 20:04. At 20:06 the lift reached the annex. Andreas locked the archive, then used the stairs to reach the terrace.
“I was only protecting my investment,” he says. Nobody in the room looks reassured.
pages.question: Build the sequence from the Count’s arrival: “When Blocula ___ the lift, Andreas ___ inside for two minutes.”
why: These forms place the events around now instead of at 20:04.
Entered gives the past reference point. Had been waiting measures the earlier activity up to that point.
Present forms move the sequence out of the finished past.
The Count’s entry is the reference event; the waiting began earlier and continued until it.

pages.title: What the camera actually proves
pages.story:
Andreas changes his story. “I’ve never locked anyone in a room.” Lestrade plays the recovered annex clip. At 20:07, Andreas is visible turning the outside lock and taking the Count’s phone from the shelf.
The general denial cannot survive one clearly recorded event. Your partner’s document supports the camera; it does not replace it.
Lestrade secures the phone and the footage. Now the problem is getting the agreement down the mountain.
pages.question: Contrast the denial about experience with the dated event that disproves it: “Andreas says he ___ anyone in. But at 20:07 tonight, he ___ the archive door from outside.”
why: Has never locked makes a claim about his experience up to now. Locked names the specific completed event at 20:07 that disproves it.
The first is not the usual form for life experience; the second unnecessarily shifts behind another past reference point.
Is locking would describe an action happening now, not the recorded event.
Never locks describes a habit, while the second clause gives a finished clock time requiring past simple here.

clue.title: The 20:07 lock footage
clue.text: The camera shows Andreas locking the archive from outside and taking Blocula’s phone. This directly supports Blocula’s account.

pages.title: The deadline is a place in time
pages.story:
Jax has the sealed agreement. Rabbit brings the final envelope from reception. Bram checks the wind meter; Walton keeps the cable car at the platform while Tensing checks every fastening.
The registrar’s assistant began waiting at 22:50. By 23:50, she will have been waiting for an hour. Your job is to make sure she is waiting for people who actually arrive.
The car’s doors close in ten minutes. Jax looks back. “One last check. Have we got the right document?”
pages.question: Express accumulated waiting and a completed future handover: “By 23:50, the assistant ___ for an hour. By 23:55, Jax ___ the agreement to her.”
options: will have been waiting / will have given
why: Future perfect continuous measures the waiting up to 23:50. Future perfect simple places the completed handover before 23:55.
Will wait does not measure duration accumulated by 23:50; will be giving leaves the handover in progress.
Will be waiting places us inside the activity but does not express its accumulated duration; has given links the handover to now.
These forms do not use the future deadlines as reference points.

pages.title: A condition worth understanding
pages.story:
The cable car pulls away. Eira and Lina watch its lights shrink against the mountain. Nobody speaks until Jax’s radio crackles: “Wind steady. We’re moving.”
Tensing explains the last condition. If the agreement reaches the registrar before midnight, the sale stops. If it arrives late, the staff will still have evidence of the crime, but the ownership dispute will take longer to settle.
This is a real possibility tonight, not an imaginary future.
pages.question: State the real condition and its expected result: “If Jax ___ in time, the registrar ___ the agreement tonight.”
why: Present simple after if plus will in the result clause expresses the real future possibility.
This is a second conditional, framing the situation as hypothetical rather than the stated real possibility.
This third conditional looks back at an unreal past, but the journey is still happening.
In this first conditional, use present simple in the if-clause rather than will.

pages.title: Who gets to tell the story?
pages.story:
Jax calls from the lower station. The assistant has the sealed agreement. Whether your evidence was strong enough for immediate registration will be clear in a moment.
Menzies asks you to handle everything quietly. Elizabeth wants the staff to hear the full truth. Blocula, wrapped in a blanket, says the choice should be theirs—but you must decide what to announce first.
Zombiella takes the microphone. For once, the whole hotel is silent.
pages.question: Contrast a completed result now with work still in progress: “Jax ___ the agreement to the assistant. The registrar ___ it at this moment.”
why: These past forms do not match the completed result now and the check happening now.
Has been giving suggests an extended activity; checks is not the requested action in progress.
Has given foregrounds the completed handover and current result. Is checking places the review in progress now.
Gives suggests a routine; checked makes the current check a finished past event.

choice.prompt: How will you handle the truth?

options.label: Tell the whole staff · share the evidence
options.effect: Give everyone the facts and a voice in the hotel’s future.

options.label: Arrange a private settlement first
options.effect: Seek a quieter deal with management before making an announcement.

pages.title: The first morning
pages.story:
The lobby clock passes midnight. Somewhere below the mountain, a stamp meets paper. Somewhere upstairs, a kettle begins to boil.
The night is over. What happens to the Grand Hotel depends on the evidence you verified, the people you protected and the truth you chose to share.

cast: Mountain guide and keeper of the hotel’s history
Trainee receptionist; copied the annex key
Small porter with a talent for narrow spaces
Quiet night cleaner; witness at the archive
Maintains the lobby clock and remembers the tunnel
Retired hotel chairwoman, staying in the winter suite
Strict shift supervisor, counting every late arrival
Holmes’s colleague; checks records and helps the rescue
Hotel security chief; secures the evidence
Night porter at the ballroom doors
Prospective buyer with a false survey
Delivery clerk and careful map reader
The Good, the Bad and the Irregular
The Good, the Bad and the Irregular
The Good, the Bad and the Irregular
The Good, the Bad and the Irregular
Retired engineer who checks the survey
Retired transport captain, running the cable car tonight
Elizabeth’s younger brother, visiting with his family
Hotel manager who accepted the false survey
Junior sailing-club member helping with blankets
Guest fishermen helping secure the landing
Guests who report the missing annex heating
Tulloch’s old colleague, helping count arrivals
Singer, witness and potential investigation partner
Lift mechanic with an alarming face and a solid alibi
Courier who must reach the registrar
guide: Alice checks the keys every evening.
An activity happening now; also a confirmed future arrangement.
Alice is checking the keys now.
A completed result, experience or state connected to now. Avoid it with a finished time such as yesterday.
She has found the key. We have known her for years.
An activity continuing to now, or recent effort with visible effects.
He has been working since seven.
past verb form / did + base verb
A finished event or state in a finished past period.
An activity in progress at a past moment; often background to an interruption.
She was singing when the lights failed.
An event completed before another past point.
He had left before the lights failed.
Duration or ongoing effort up to a past point.
He had been waiting for two minutes when the Count arrived.
Predictions, promises, offers and decisions made now.
I will carry the folder for you.
An activity in progress at a future time.
At eleven, he will be testing the circuit.
Completion before or by a future point.
By 23:20, he will have repaired the lock.
Duration of an activity measured up to a future point.
At midnight, he will have been working for five hours.
am / is / are going to + base verb
An existing plan or a prediction supported by present evidence. Will and going to can overlap; context matters.
Look at that beam! It is going to fall.
was / were going to + base verb
An intention or expectation viewed from the past; it may or may not happen.
Andreas was going to close the hotel.
A past habit or state that is no longer true.
Tensing used to deliver bags there.
He is used to working in tunnels.
am / is / are being + past participle
An action being done to the subject now.
A completed action affecting the subject, with a result now.
